recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Revisit only if OO opens a separate editorial cleanup for old example comments or legacy binding registry material; no current-spec fix is needed for FHIR-7154.
issue_request: FHIR-7154 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request against DSTU1 Observation. It challenged Observation.reliability as ill-defined and not useful as a discrete field; the accepted motion was to remove the element and solicit more specific device requirements.
initial_application: Git commit 54f14f427c6d24a74a89a58246d2f25abce02fc4 explicitly applied the issue with subject '#7154 remove reliability from Observation', removing the generated Observation.reliability spreadsheet row and updating Observation notes/examples so the element no longer appeared as a resource element.
additional_context: Observation is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition has no Observation.reliability element; related Jira FHIR-7216 is a duplicate of FHIR-7154, while FHIR-3002 and FHIR-5565 are earlier reliability changes superseded by the later removal. Remaining current-source reliability matches are incidental prose, example XML comments, legacy binding registry text, or unrelated QUICK/library material and do not reintroduce the element.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current authoritative Observation StructureDefinition already satisfies the accepted removal. Editing incidental comments or legacy non-Observation references would be broader than the Jira decision and would not change current conformance expectations.
